thread:
julia: running the AWQ vs GPTQ bakeoff on the new-7B variant, seeing weird tail errors on a subset of prompts. shallow summary: AWQ ~1.7% avg ppl delta, GPTQ ~1.1% but a few prompts blow up.
samir: can you paste the distribution? is it per-layer or per-token?
julia: mostly per-layer spikes around layers 8-11. per-token spikes line up with long-tail tokens (rare names). attaching quick stats.
ben: hmm, that sounds like channel-wise outliers not captured by global quant. did you try per-channel clamp or channel-wise absmax rescale?
julia: tried global clip=3.0 -> reduces avg delta but still 5/120 prompts huge degradation. logs:
```
prompt_id: 87
layer: 9
channel: 204
max_act: 12.4
quant_error: 0.82
```
lei: try surgical skip for the offending channels or fall back to FP8 on those layers. AWQ has cheaper perf but less robust to big activations.
samir: +1 for hybrid: run AWQ by default, but mark channels with max_act>8 for GPTQ/FP16. automation idea: collect per-channel max_act histogram during calibration, then generate a skiplist.
julia: prototype config I used:
```
quant_profile:
  default: awq
  fallbacks:
    - condition: max_act > 8.0
      method: gptq
    - condition: layer in [8,9,10]
      method: fp16
```
ben: looks good. also consider per-channel scaling pre-quant: scale = max(channel_abs)/target, clamp after. small patch we used earlier:
```
scale = min(1.0, 2.5 / max_abs)
weights[channel] *= scale
```
lei: one more: measure KLDelta on logits per-prompt to detect regressions early; roll back if KLD > 0.02 on a sliding window.
eval-bot: AWQ-run-1925009999: eval set (n=500) -> ppl_delta 1.72%, kl_mean 0.009, worst10_avg_ppl_delta 14.3% (ids: 87, 203, 342, ...)
julia: thanks @eval-bot. for the worst ones, I'll dump activations and run a channel surgery pass. plan: 1) collect per-channel max_abs during calibration 2) auto-generate skiplist for channels with top 0.5% outliers 3) re-run AWQ with pre-scale and channel clamp 4) if still bad, fallback layer->FP16
samir: could we make the threshold adaptive by layer (some layers tolerate higher max_act)?
ben: yes — compute layer-specific 95th percentile and set threshold = max(8.0, 1.5 * p95[layer])
julia: good call. I'll run nightly job that emits a csv of layer,p95,top_channels and push results here tomorrow morning. anyone want to join the quick triage at 10:30am PST?
lei: I can join.
samir: me too.
ben: ping me if you need the channel-surgery script; I can drop it into the repo.
julia: awesome — thanks team. leaving notes in the bakeoff doc and will post the CSV and example dumps in the thread.
